verses.1: After stopping the noise, Paul sent his disciples away and then went to Macedonia.
verses.2: After going through those places, and after persuading them with many words, he went to Greece.
verses.3: He spent three months in preparation. After the Jews’ plan to send him to Syria was rejected, it was decided that he should be sent through Macedonia instead.
verses.4: In addition to him, there were also Sopatros of Pyrrha from Veria, Aristarchus from Thessalonica, and Secondus. There was also Gaius of Derba and Timotheus. In Asia, there were Tichikos and Trofimus.
verses.5: And these people came and left us in Tria.
verses.6: We traveled from Philippi for several days, and then we came to them in Traya, after five days. In total, it took us seven days to get there.
verses.7: On one of the Sabbath days, Paul decided to divide up the bread among us, so that we could eat it together at the end of the day. He postponed speaking until midday.
verses.8: And they were lamps of light in the upper room where we were gathered together.
verses.9: He sat on the throne, under the name of Eutychus. He fell asleep deeply, lost in thoughts about Paul’s words. After falling asleep, he fell from the third floor and died.
verses.10: But when Paul stepped forward, he also said, “Do not be afraid. For his soul is in him.”
verses.11: Then he raised and cut the bread, ate it in due course, and continued to eat until he was full.
verses.12: They brought the child alive, and they were brought before them without any delay.
verses.13: We went ahead to the ship, and then we boarded the boat. From there, we were to pick up Paul. This was how he was scheduled to travel.
verses.14: And as we were on our way to Hestia, we took him with us and went to Mitylene.
verses.15: From there, we sailed along the coast and stopped by Chios. From there, we continued to Samos. And from there, we arrived in Miletus.
verses.16: For Paul really wanted to extend the Epistle, so that he wouldn’t have to spend time in Asia. He rushed forward, hoping that it would be possible for him to deliver the Epistle to Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
verses.17: After sending them from Miletus to Ephesus, he also asked for the elders of the church to come along with him.
verses.18: And when they came before him, he said to them, “You have been afraid from the first day that I entered Asia, how I managed to do everything with you for so long.”
verses.19: working for the Lord with complete humility, and offering thanks and praise to Him. I also endured many hardships during the times when I was working on the plans of the Jews.
verses.20: As I have not omitted anything that is relevant to your benefit; I will teach you publicly and in private homes.
verses.21: He protested against the Jewish and Greek people’s belief in God, and their faith in our Lord Jesus.
verses.22: And now, I see that I am being led by the Spirit towards Jerusalem. What I will encounter there, I do not know.
verses.23: In addition, the holy spirit, according to the people who complain about this city, says that it will bring suffering and sorrow to me.
verses.24: But I will make the soul honorable by saying nothing else. I will complete my path and fulfill the duty that I have taken from the Lord Jesus. I will also spread the good news of God’s grace.
verses.25: And now I know that you all no longer see my face, those among whom I went to proclaim the kingdom.
verses.26: For I testify to you today that I am pure from all impurities.
verses.27: For I did not wish to prevent you from carrying out all of God’s will.
verses.28: Be careful of yourselves and also of all those who are in charge of the church. They are those who have the holy spirit to guide them. They are responsible for governing the church of God, which He has established through His own blood.
verses.29: I know that after my departure, wolves will come to you. They won’t be afraid of the shepherd.
verses.30: And from among you, there will be men who will speak in a way that is completely wrongful, and who will try to get back their students.
verses.31: Therefore, hurry up, and remember that I did not stop giving gifts to each one of them for three nights and days.
verses.32: And what I present to you now is the God and His word. It is a power that can be used to establish and give inheritance to all those who are chosen by Him.
verses.33: I don’t desire either silver or gold, nor any kind of jewelry.
verses.34: You must know that it was their hands that served me and those who were with me in need.
verses.35: I have always reminded you that when you give, you must also take into account the needs of those who are weaker than you. You should also remember the words of Lord Jesus: “It is better to give than to receive.”
verses.36: And while he was speaking these things, he also touched his knees together with all of them.
verses.37: But it became possible to laugh at all of them. And when they fell onto Paul’s neck, they laughed at him.
verses.38: The most distressed of them all agreed with this statement, saying that his face should no longer be considered worthy of attention. They then sent him back onto the ship.
